sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.content: Beyond recursion, a far more efficient approach is **dynamic programming** (Bottom-Up DP): compute answers from small to large and [[primary|record]] each subproblem's result.
items: Build a 1D array dp where **dp[i]** is the i-th Fibonacci number
**Transition**: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2] — each cell depends only on the previous two
Scan left to right so every subproblem is **computed exactly once**

Filling the table from small to large is called [[primary|Tabulation]] (bottom-up); keeping the recursion and adding a cache, [[primary|Memoization]] (top-down), also trades space for time — both share the same recurrence

sections.heading: Operation Complexity
sections.content: Compared with the exponential recursive version, DP eliminates all repeated work and drastically lowers the cost.
items: **Time complexity**: [[success|O(n)]] — each cell is computed once
**Space complexity**: [[warning|O(n)]] — an array of length n is required
Versus naive recursion's [[danger|O(2ⁿ)]], the gap widens sharply as n grows

sections.heading: What It Optimizes
sections.content: Since each cell depends only on the previous two, the whole array need not be kept.
items: **Rolling variables**: keep only the latest two values, reducing space to [[success|O(1)]]
**Top-Down memoization**: keep the recursive form and cache results to avoid recomputation
Once you grasp the pattern, it extends to problems like **Climbing Stairs** with the same recurrence
